title: Restriction of refinement factors on the scalar unit
statement: Fix $k$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, their inclusion $i$ and the finite-free restriction assertion $s$ [lem-coef-finite-free-system-restriction]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes and let $M$ be a normalized lower-coefficient derived system with bounded constructible finite-Tor levels [def-coef-system-scalar-projection-data]. The lower refinement comparisons satisfy RefinementCoherence. For every proper refinement $r:c_1\to c_2$, the specified lower refinement gamma at $M$ and upper refinement gamma at $T_XM$ are invertible. Restriction of the upper theta, followed by the target compact-support restriction comparison, equals the source compact-support restriction comparison followed by lower theta at $U_XT_XM$. Lower theta is natural at the scalar unit $\eta_M:M\to U_XT_XM$. This assertion concerns geometric restriction factors and the scalar unit only; it asserts neither the scalar-comparison refinement square nor upper-tower refinement coherence.

source.place: Ordinary direct image: finite free coefficient extension follows from finite sums; Compactly supported direct image: combine proper and open comparisons and commute with refinement; Construction of comparison maps: canonical conjugates and mates. Explicit coherent strict-system argument as in lem-coef-system-scalar-projection-identification.

proof.text: Apply the existing system compactification refinement theorem to the lower DVR tower at M. Identify its ordinary and derived operations with the specified constant-system operations by their section formulas and adjunction normalization. The levelwise bounded constructible hypothesis follows from the finite-Tor constructible domain. This proves lower gamma invertibility and the lower identity, composition, independence and cocycle laws.

The single reduced integral basis identifies U T M with a finite sum of M. The sum remains normalized with bounded constructible finite-Tor levels, with no bound uniform in n. Apply the lower gamma invertibility theorem to that sum. Restriction preserves gamma, its identity direct-image factor and direct-image compositors. As exact restriction reflects isomorphisms on cohomology, upper gamma at T M is invertible, also for ramified upper towers. Applying restriction to the inverse then proves the theta restriction square. Naturality of the geometric gamma and compositor, and the inverse naturality square on these inputs, gives lower theta naturality at the scalar unit.
